44:1: Interpretation of Surat Ad-Dukhan It is Meccan Al-Tirmidhi said: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, Zaid ibn Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Khatham, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Ha Mim Ad-Dukhan at night, seventy thousand angels will ask forgiveness for him in the morning. Then he said: It is strange. We do not know it except from this source, and Umar ibn Abi Khatham is considered weak. Al-Bukhari said: His hadith is objectionable. Then he said: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Kufi told us, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Hisham Abu Al-Miqdam, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Ha-Mim Ad-Dukhan on the night of Friday will be forgiven. Then he said: It is strange, we do not know it except from this source, and Hisham Abu Al-Miqdam is considered weak, and Al-Hasan did not hear it from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him. This is what Ayoub, Yunus bin Ubaid, and Ali bin Zaid, may God have mercy on them all, said. In Musnad Al-Bazzar, on the authority of Abu Al-Tufail Amir bin Wathilah, on the authority of Zaid bin Haritha, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ibn Sayyad: I have hidden something, what is it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hid Surat Ad-Dukhan for him, and he said: It is smoke. So he said: Be gone, what God wills will be, then he left. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty says, informing us about the Noble Qur’an, that He revealed it on a blessed night, which is the Night of Decree, as He the Almighty said: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And that was in the month of Ramadan, as He the Almighty said: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur’an. We have already mentioned in the hadiths that were reported in Surat Al-Baqarah what suffices not to repeat. Whoever says that it is the night of the middle of Sha’ban, as narrated from Ikrimah, has missed the point, because the text of the Qur’an states that it is in Ramadan. The hadith that Abdullah ibn Salih narrated from Al-Layth from Aqeel from Al-Zuhri, ‘Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Mughirah ibn Al-Akhns told me that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Deaths are cut off from one Sha’ban to the next, to the extent that a man marries and has a child born to him while his name has been brought out among the dead. This is a mursal hadith, and similar hadiths do not contradict the texts. God the Almighty said: Indeed, We were to warn, meaning, We were to teach them what would benefit and harm them according to the Shari’ah, so that God’s proof would be established against His servants. His saying: In it every wise matter is decreed, meaning on the Night of Decree, from the Preserved Tablet to the scribes, the matter of the year is decreed, and what will be in it of terms and provisions and what will be in it until its end. Thus it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Al-Dahhak and more than one of the early Muslims. The words of God, the Most High, Wise mean well-established that cannot be changed or altered. That is why the Most High said, A command from Us meaning everything that happens and is decreed by God, the Most High, and that which He reveals is by His command, permission and knowledge. Indeed, We were sending meaning to the people a Messenger who would recite to them the clear verses of God, for there was a dire need for him. That is why God, the Most High, said, “A mercy from your Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing. Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them” meaning the One who sent down the Qur’an is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, their Creator, their Owner and what is in them. If you should be certain meaning if you were certain. Then God, the Most High, said, “There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death. Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.” This verse is like the words of God, the Most High, “Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death’” 10:17.

44:9: God the Almighty says: Rather, these polytheists are in doubt, playing. That is, the certain truth has come to them, and they are doubting it and are not believing in it. Then the Almighty said, threatening and warning them: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A’mash said, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha Muslim ibn Subayh, on the authority of Masruq, who said: “We entered the mosque, meaning the mosque of Kufa at the gates of Kinda, and there was a man narrating to his companions: “The Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke.” Do you know what that smoke is? That is smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection and will take over the hearing and sight of the hypocrites, and it will take over the believers like a cold. He said: So we went to Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him and mentioned that to him, and he was lying down. He was startled, so he sat up and said: God the Almighty said to your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward, nor am I of the pretenders.” It is part of knowledge for a man to say about something he does not know, God knows best. I will tell you about that. When the Quraysh delayed embracing Islam and resisted the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he invoked upon them years like the years of Joseph, and they were afflicted with hardship and hunger until they ate bones and dead meat. They would raise their eyes to the sky but would see nothing but smoke. In another narration, a man would look to the sky and see what was between him and it like smoke because of the hardship. God the Almighty said: “Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, enveloping the people. This is a painful torment.” So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came and it was said: O Messenger of God, ask God for rain for Mudar, for they have perished. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked for rain for them, but they were given rain. Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little; indeed, you will return. Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him said: “The punishment will be removed from them on the Day of Resurrection, and when they were granted prosperity, they returned to their state. Then God the Almighty revealed: “The Day We will strike with the greatest strike. Indeed, We will take retribution.” He said: He meant the Day of Badr. Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him said: “Five have already passed: the smoke, the Romans, the moon, the strike, and the binding.” This hadith is included in the two Sahihs and Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad. It is also found in at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa’i in their commentaries, and in Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim through various chains of narration on the authority of al-A’mash. A group of the Salaf, such as Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, Ibrahim an-Nakha’i, ad-Dahhak, and Atiyah al-Awfi, agreed with Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him on interpreting the verse in this way, and that the smoke has passed.” This is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ja'far ibn Musafir told us, Yahya ibn Hassan told us, Ibn Lahi'ah told us, Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj told us regarding the words of God Almighty: The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, he said: It was the day of the conquest of Mecca. This statement is very strange, indeed reprehensible. Others said that the smoke has not yet passed, rather it is one of the signs of the Hour, as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Sarihah Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) looked down upon us from Arafah while we were discussing the Hour. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the beast, the emergence of Gog and Magog, the emergence of Jesus, son of Mary, the Antichrist, and three landslides: one in the east, one in the west, and one in the Arabian Peninsula, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden and drive the people - or gather the people - and spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and rest with them wherever they rest." Muslim is the only one to report it in his Sahih. In the two Sahihs, it is reported that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Ibn Sayyad: I have hidden something for you. He said: It is smoke. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Be gone, for you will not exceed your limit. He said: And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) hid for him: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. This indicates that he is one of the awaited ones. Ibn Sayyad is a fortune-teller in the manner of soothsayers using the tongue of the jinn, and they confuse the phrase. That is why he said: It is smoke, meaning smoke. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knew its substance and that it was Satanic, so he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Be gone, for you will not exceed your limit. Then Ibn Jarir said: Issam bin Rawad bin Al Jarrah told me, my father told us, Sufyan bin Abi Saeed Al Thawri told us, Mansur bin Al Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of Rib'i bin Harash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah bin Al Yaman may God be pleased with him say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The first of the signs will be the Antichrist and the descent of Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon them both), and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden, Abyan, driving the people to the place of assembly, resting with them when they say, and the smoke - Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, what is the smoke? A group of the Salaf, such as Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, Ibrahim an-Nakha’i, ad-Dahhak, and Atiyah al-Awfi, agreed with Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him on interpreting the verse in this way, and that the smoke has passed.” This is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ja'far ibn Musafir told us, Yahya ibn Hassan told us, Ibn Lahi'ah told us, Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj told us regarding the words of God Almighty: The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, he said: It was the day of the conquest of Mecca. This statement is very strange, indeed reprehensible. Others said that the smoke has not yet passed, rather it is one of the signs of the Hour, as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Sarihah Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) looked down upon us from Arafah while we were discussing the Hour. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the beast, the emergence of Gog and Magog, the emergence of Jesus, son of Mary, the Antichrist, and three landslides: one in the east, one in the west, and one in the Arabian Peninsula, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden and drive the people - or gather the people - and spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and rest with them wherever they rest." Muslim is the only one to report it in his Sahih. In the two Sahihs, it is reported that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Ibn Sayyad: I have hidden something for you. He said: It is smoke. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Be gone, for you will not exceed your limit. He said: And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) hid for him: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. This indicates that he is one of the awaited ones. Ibn Sayyad is a fortune-teller in the manner of soothsayers using the tongue of the jinn, and they confuse the phrase. That is why he said: It is smoke, meaning smoke. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knew its substance and that it was Satanic, so he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Be gone, for you will not exceed your limit. Then Ibn Jarir said: Issam bin Rawad bin Al Jarrah told me, my father told us, Sufyan bin Abi Saeed Al Thawri told us, Mansur bin Al Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of Rib'i bin Harash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah bin Al Yaman may God be pleased with him say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The first of the signs will be the Antichrist and the descent of Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon them both), and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden, Abyan, driving the people to the place of assembly, resting with them when they say, and the smoke - Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, what is the smoke? So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recited this verse: 'Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, enveloping the people. This is a painful punishment' - that will fill the space between the east and the west and will remain for forty days and nights. As for the believer, it will affect him like a cold, and as for the disbeliever, it will be like a drunkard, coming out of his nostrils, ears, and anus." Ibn Jarir said: If this hadith was authentic, it would have been decisive. I did not attest to its authenticity because Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me that he asked some scholars about this hadith, Did he hear it from Sufyan? He said: No. I said: Did you read it to him? He said: No. I said: Should I read it to him while you are present and he will acknowledge it? He said: No. I said: Then where did you get it from? He said: Some people brought it to me and presented it to me and said, ‘Listen to it from us.’ So they read it to me and then went and narrated it from me, or something to that effect. Ibn Jarir did well with this hadith here, as it is fabricated with this chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir cited it frequently in many places in this commentary, and it contains many objectionable matters, especially at the beginning of Surah Bani Isra’il when mentioning al-Masjid al-Aqsa. And God knows best. Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Awf told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Your Lord has warned you of three things: the smoke will overtake the believer like a cold, and the disbeliever will be swollen until it comes out of every ear. The second is the beast, and the third is the Antichrist.” At-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Hashim ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash, and this is a good chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Sufyan told us, Al-Walid told us, Khalil told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The smoke will stir up the people. As for the believer, it will overtake him like a cold, and as for the disbeliever, it will swell until it comes out of every ear.” It was narrated by Saeed bin Abi Aruba on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, as an interrupted chain of transmission. Saeed bin Awf narrated the same on the authority of Al-Hasan. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah bin Saleh bin Muslim told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The verse of the smoke has not yet happened. It will affect the believer like a cold, and it will make the unbeliever sneeze until he is exhausted. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Malekah, who said: I went to Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, one day, and he said: I did not sleep last night until morning. I said: Why? He said: They said the comet appeared, and I was afraid that the smoke had come, so I did not sleep until morning. Thus, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abi Omar, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and he mentioned it. This is a sound chain of transmission going back to Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, the scholar of this nation and the interpreter of the Qur’an. This is also the statement of those who agreed with him from the Companions and Followers, may God be pleased with them all, along with the authentic and hasan hadiths and others that they mentioned, which contain convincing evidence and clear proof that the smoke is one of the awaited signs, even though it is apparent in the Qur’an. God Almighty said: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, meaning clear and obvious, visible to everyone. According to what Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, interpreted it, it is only an image that they saw in their eyes due to the intensity of hunger and effort. This is also the statement of God Almighty: It covers the people, meaning it covers them and encompasses them. If it were an imaginary matter specific to the polytheist people of Mecca, then it would not have been said in it: It covers the people. And the Almighty’s saying: This is a painful torment means that it will be said to them as a rebuke and a rebuke, like His saying: The Day they are summoned to the fire of Hell, it will be summoned, ‘This is the Fire which you used to deny.’ Or some of them will say that to each other. And His saying, the Most High: “Our Lord, remove from us the punishment. Indeed, we are believers,” meaning that the disbelievers will say when they see the torment and punishment of God, asking Him to lift it and remove it from them, like His saying, the Most Great: And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, ‘Oh, would that we could be sent back and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers.’ And likewise His saying, the Most High: “And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, ‘Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will respond to Your call and follow the messengers.’ Did you not swear before that there would be no removal for you?’” And thus the Almighty said here: How can they be reminded when there has come to them a clear Messenger? Indeed, you will return.” has two possible meanings: One that the Almighty is saying, And if We removed the punishment from you and returned you to the worldly home, you would return to the state you were in of disbelief and denial, as in His statement: And if We had mercy on them and removed the harm that was upon them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly. The second that what is meant is that We will delay the punishment for you for a little after its causes have been established and it has reached you, and you will continue in your state of transgression and misguidance. 44:17: God the Almighty says: And We had already tested before these polytheists the people of Pharaoh, who were the Copts of Egypt, “And there came to them a noble Messenger, meaning Moses, the one who spoke to Him, peace and blessings be upon him, that they should hand over to Me the servants of God, as God the Almighty says: “So send with us the Children of Israel and do not punish them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord, and peace be upon him who follows the guidance.” And God the Almighty says: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger, meaning, one who is trusted with what he conveys to you. And God the Almighty says: And that you do not exalt yourselves above God, meaning, do not be arrogant about following His signs, submitting to His proofs, and believing in His evidence, as God the Almighty says: Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] humiliated. “Indeed, I have come to you with a clear authority,” meaning, with an apparent and clear proof, which is what God the Almighty sent him with of clear signs and decisive evidence. And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord lest you stone me. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and Abu Saleh said: It means stoning with the tongue, which is cursing. Qatada said: Stoning with stones means I seek refuge in God who created me and you from you reaching me with evil words or deeds. And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone. That is, do not interfere with me and leave the matter between me and you peacefully until God judges between us. When his stay among them was prolonged and he established God’s proofs against them, All of this only increased their disbelief and stubbornness. He called upon his Lord against them with a call that was implemented upon them, as the Blessed and Most High said: “And Moses said, ‘Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his establishment adornments and wealth in the life of this world, [saying], “Our Lord, that they may mislead [others] from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.” He said, Indeed, your prayer has been answered, so remain steadfast. But they were robbed of all of that in one morning, and they departed this world and went to Hell, and what an evil destination that is. The land of Egypt and those Pharaonic crops and the Coptic kingdoms were taken over by the Children of Israel, as God Almighty said: Thus did We give them as an inheritance to the Children of Israel. And He said in this other verse: "And We gave as an inheritance to the people who had been oppressed the eastern regions of the land and the western regions which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they patiently endured. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been making and what they had been constructing." And God the Almighty said here: Likewise, and We gave it as an inheritance to another people, and they are the Children of Israel, as mentioned above. And His statement, the Most High: So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, means they had no righteous deeds that would ascend to the gates of heaven and weep over their loss, nor did they have places on earth where they worshipped God that were lost to them. For this reason, they deserved not to be looked at or delayed because of their disbelief, crimes, insolence, and stubbornness. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Ishaq Al-Basri told us, Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah told us, Yazid Al-Raqashi told me, Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him told me that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “There is no servant of God but that he has two gates in the heaven: a gate from which his provision comes out, and a gate from which his deeds and words enter. So when he dies, they miss him and weep over him.” He recited this verse: So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them, and mentioned that they had not done any righteous deeds on earth for which they would be wept for, and that no good words or deeds from their words or deeds ascended to the heavens for them to be visited and for them to be wept for. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubaydah, who is al-Rabdhi. Ibn Jarir said: Yahya ibn Talhah told me, Isa ibn Yunus told me, on the authority of Safwan ibn Amr, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd al-Hadrami, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange as it began. Beware, there is no strangeness for a believer. No believer dies in a strange land in which his mourners are absent from him, except that the heavens and the earth weep for him.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: So neither the heavens nor the earth wept for them, and then he said: They do not weep for the disbeliever. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Issam told us, Abu Ahmad - meaning Al-Zubayri - told us, Al-Ala ibn Salih told us, on the authority of Al-Minhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Ibad ibn Abdullah, who said: A man asked Ali may God be pleased with him: Do the heavens and the earth weep for anyone? He said to him: You have asked me about something that no one before you has asked me about. There is no servant of God but that he has a place of prayer on earth and an ascent for his deeds from the heavens. The people of Pharaoh had no righteous deeds on earth nor any deeds that ascend to the heavens. Then Ali may God be pleased with him recited: So the heaven and the earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Talq ibn Ghannam told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Minhal, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both and said: O Abu Abbas, what do you think of the statement of God the Most High: So the heaven and the earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved. Do the heavens and the earth weep for anyone? He, may God be pleased with him, said: Yes, there is no one among creation except that he has a door in the heavens from which his sustenance descends and through which his deeds ascend. So when a believer dies and his door in the heavens through which his deeds ascended and his sustenance descended is closed, and he loses him, the heavens weep for him. And when his place of prayer in the land in which he used to pray and remember God, the Almighty, the Majestic, loses him, the heavens and the earth weep for him. The people of Pharaoh had no good traces on the earth and no good from them ascended to God, the Almighty, the Majestic, so the heavens and the earth did not weep for them. Al-Awfi narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Yahya al-Qattat from Mujahid from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both who said: It was said that the earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings. Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair and others said the same. Mujahid also said: No believer dies except that the heavens and the earth weep for him for forty mornings. I said to him: Does the earth weep? He said: Are you amazed? Why would the earth not weep for a servant who used to fill it with bowing and prostration? Why would the heavens not weep for a servant whose glorification and praise therein made a buzz like the buzzing of bees? Qatada said: They were too insignificant to God the Almighty for the heavens and the earth to weep for them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin al-Husayn narrated to us, Abd al-Salam bin Asim narrated to us, Ishaq bin Ismail narrated to us, al-Mustawrid bin Sabeq narrated to us from Ubayd al-Maktab from Ibrahim who said: The heavens have only wept for two people since the beginning of the world. I said to Ubayd: Do not the heavens and the earth weep for the believer? He said: That is his station where his deeds ascend. He said: Do you know what the weeping of the heavens is? I said: No. He said: It turns red and becomes a rose like oil. When Yahya ibn Zakariya, peace be upon him, was killed, the sky turned red and dripped blood. When al-Husayn ibn Ali, may God be pleased with them both, was killed, the sky turned red. And Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Abu Ghassan Muhammad bin Amr Zanij told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, who said: When Al-Hussein bin Ali, may God be pleased with them both, was killed, the horizons of the sky turned red for four months. Yazid said: Its redness is its weeping. Al-Suddi said the same in Al-Kabir. Ata Al-Khurasani said: Its weeping is that its edges turn red. They also mentioned regarding the killing of Al-Hussein, may God be pleased with him, that no stone was turned over that day except that fresh blood was found beneath it, and that the sun was eclipsed, the horizon turned red, and stones fell. There is consideration for each of that, and it appears that it is from the foolishness and lies of the Shiites to magnify the matter, and there is no doubt that it is great, but what they fabricated and lied about did not happen. Something greater than the killing of Al-Hussein, may God be pleased with him, did happen, and nothing of what they mentioned happened. His father, Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, was killed, and he was better than him according to consensus, and none of that happened. Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, was killed while besieged and wronged, and none of that happened. And Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him was killed in the mihrab during the dawn prayer, as if no calamity had befallen the Muslims before that and none of that had happened. And this is the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who is the master of mankind in this world and the hereafter. On the day he died, none of what they mentioned happened. And on the day Ibrahim, the son of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), died, the sun eclipsed and the people said: It eclipsed because of the death of Ibrahim! So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) led them in the eclipse prayer and delivered a sermon and explained to them that the sun and moon do not eclipse because of the death or life of anyone. And the saying of God, the Blessed and Most High: “And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment * From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty and among the transgressors.” God, the Most High, is showing them His gratitude for this, as He saved them from what they were in of Pharaoh’s humiliation and degradation of them, and his subjecting them to humiliating and difficult tasks. And the saying of God, the Most High: “From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty” means arrogant, tyrannical, and stubborn, as God, the Almighty, says: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and His saying, the Most Great: But they were arrogant and were a haughty people among the transgressors, meaning extravagant in his affairs and foolish in his own opinion. And the saying of God, the Most High: And We certainly chose them, with knowledge, over the worlds. Mujahid said: We chose them, with knowledge, over the worlds over those who were among him. Qatada said: They were chosen over the people of their time. It was said that every time has a scholar. This is like the saying of God the Almighty: {He said, O Moses, indeed I have chosen you over mankind} meaning the people of his time. This is like His saying to Mary, peace be upon her: {And He chose you over the women of the worlds”} meaning in her time. Khadija, may God be pleased with her, was either better than her or equal to her in virtue, and so was Asiya bint Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh. The virtue of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, over women is like the virtue of tharid over all other foods. And the saying of God the Almighty: {And We gave them of the signs} meaning the arguments, proofs and miracles in which was a clear trial meaning a clear and obvious test for whoever follows its guidance.
44:34: God Almighty says, denouncing the polytheists for their denial of resurrection and the afterlife, and that there is nothing but this worldly life and no life after death, no resurrection and no revival. They argue with their past fathers who passed away and did not return. If resurrection is true, Then bring our fathers, if you should be truthful. This is a false argument and a corrupt semblance, because the afterlife is only on the Day of Resurrection, not in this worldly abode, but after it has passed away and is empty. God will create the worlds anew, and will make the wrongdoers fuel for the fire of Hell, on the day you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. Then God Almighty said, threatening them, warning them, and warning them of His punishment that cannot be repelled, as happened to those like them and their peers among the polytheists who denied the afterlife, such as the people of Tubba’, who are Saba’, when God Almighty destroyed them, ruined their land, scattered them throughout the lands, and dispersed them to scattered fragments, as was mentioned in Surat Saba’, which begins with the denial of the polytheists. For the Resurrection, and likewise here He likened them to those, and they were Arabs from Qahtan, just as these are Arabs from Adnan, and the Himyar, who are Saba, whenever a man ruled among them, they named him Tubba, just as it is said Khosrau for the one who ruled Persia, and Caesar for the one who ruled Rome, and Pharaoh for the one who ruled Egypt as an infidel, and Negus for the one who ruled Abyssinia, and other prominent races. But it happened that some of their followers left Yemen and traveled through the country until they reached Samarkand. His kingdom grew stronger, his authority and army became great, his kingdom and country expanded, and his subjects increased. He was the one who conquered Al-Hirah. It happened that he passed by the Prophet’s city during the days of ignorance. He wanted to fight its people, but they prevented him and fought him during the day, and they kept him waiting at night. He felt ashamed of them and refrained from them. He took with him two Jewish rabbis who had advised him and told him that he had no way to this city, as it was the migration of a prophet who would come at the end of time. So he returned from it and took them with him to the country of Yemen. When he passed by Mecca, he wanted to demolish the Kaaba, but they also forbade him from that and told him of the greatness of this house, and that it was built by Abraham, peace be upon him, and that he would have a great affair at the hands of that prophet sent at the end of time. So he glorified it and circumambulated it and covered it with robes, tapestries, and rabbis. Then he returned to Yemen and called its people to Judaism with him. At that time, the religion of Moses, peace be upon him, had those who would… From the guidance before the mission of Jesus, peace be upon him, so the majority of the people of Yemen converted to Judaism with him. The story was mentioned in full by Imam Muhammad bin Ishaq in his book, Al-Seerah, and Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir gave a comprehensive biography of him in his history in which he included many things that we mentioned and what we did not mention. He mentioned that he was the king of Damascus and that whenever he reviewed the horses, they would appear before him from Damascus to Yemen. Then he cited from the path of Abd Al-Razzaq from Muammar from Ibn Abi Dhi’b from Al-Maqburi from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace be upon him, who said: I do not know if the borders are pure for its people or not? I do not know if Tubba was cursed or not? I do not know if Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet or a king? Another said, Was Ezra a prophet or not? Thus, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Dhahrani on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq. Al-Daraqutni said: Abd al-Razzaq was the only one to narrate it. Then Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kurayb on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I do not know whether Ezra was a prophet or not? I do not know whether the accursed one was Tubba’ or not? Then he mentioned what was narrated regarding the prohibition of insulting and cursing him, as will come later, God willing. And it seems that - and God knows best - he was a disbeliever, then he converted to Islam and followed the religion of Moses at the hands of one of the Jewish rabbis of that time, who was on the truth before the mission of Jesus (peace be upon him). He performed Hajj during the time of the Jurhumites, and he was clothed in silk and ink, and six thousand camels were slaughtered near him, and he was honored and respected. Then he returned to Yemen. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated his story in full, through various lengthy and detailed chains of transmission on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abdullah ibn Salam, and Abdullah ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them, and Ka'b al-Ahbar, to whom the reference is made in all of this, and also to Abdullah ibn Salam, who is more established, older, and more knowledgeable. His story was also narrated by Wahb ibn Munabbih and Muhammad ibn Ishaq in the Seerah, as is well-known therein. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mixed up in some contexts the biography of this Tubba’ with the biography of another who came after him by a long time. This Tubba’ referred to in the Qur’an converted his people to Islam at his hands, then when he died, they returned after him to the worship of fire and idols, so God punished them as He mentioned in Surah Saba’. We have already explained their story there, praise and thanks be to God. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Tubba’ covered the Ka’bah, and Sa’id used to forbid cursing him. This Tubba’ is the middle Tubba’, and his name is As’ad Abu Kurayb ibn Malikikarb al-Yamani. They mentioned that he ruled over his people for three hundred and twenty-six years, and there was no one in Himyar who ruled longer than him. He died about seven hundred years before the mission of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). They mentioned that when the two rabbis from the Jews of Medina mentioned to him that this town was the place where a prophet named Ahmad would migrate at the end of time, he composed a poem about that and entrusted it to the people of Medina, who would pass it on and narrate it from generation to generation. Among those who memorized it was Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd, in whose house the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stayed, and it is: I testify that Ahmad is a messenger from God, the Creator of all souls. If my life had been extended to his, I would have been his minister and cousin. I fought his enemies with the sword and relieved his chest of all sorrow Ibn Abi Al-Dunya mentioned that a grave was dug in Sana’a during Islam and two healthy women were found in it, and at their heads was a silver tablet written in gold: This is the grave of Huyayy and Tamis. It was narrated that Huyayy and Tamadur, the daughters of Tubba’, died while bearing witness that there is no god but God and that they do not associate anything with Him. The righteous before them died on that basis. We have also mentioned poetry about this in Surah Saba’. Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that Ka’b used to say about Tubba’ a description of a righteous man: God, the Most High, blamed his people but did not blame him. He said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, used to say: Do not revile Tubba’, for he was a righteous man. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Safwan told us, Al-Walid told us, Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Abu Zur’ah - meaning Amr ibn Jabir Al-Hadrami - who said: I heard Sahl ibn Sa’d Al-Sa’idi, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not revile Tubba’, for he had embraced Islam. It was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad on the authority of Hasan ibn Musa on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah. At-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Abar told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Barzah told us, Mu’ammil ibn Isma’il told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Samak ibn Harb on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: Do not curse Tubba, for he has become Muslim. Abd al-Razzaq also said: Mu’ammar told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b on the authority of al-Maqburi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I do not know whether Tubba was a prophet or not. This chain of transmission was presented earlier on the authority of Ibn Abi Hatim, as Ibn Asakir included it: I do not know whether Tubba was cursed or not. And God knows best. Ibn Asakir narrated it on the authority of Zakariya ibn Yahya al-Badi on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Abdul Razzaq said: Imran Abu Al-Hudhayl told us, Tamim bin Abdul Rahman told me, he said: Ata bin Abi Rabah said: Do not insult Tubba’, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade insulting him, and God Almighty knows best.

It happened that he passed by the Prophet’s city during the days of ignorance. He wanted to fight its people, but they prevented him and fought him during the day, and they kept him waiting at night. He felt ashamed of them and refrained from them. He took with him two Jewish rabbis who had advised him and told him that he had no way to this city, as it was the migration of a prophet who would come at the end of time. So he returned from it and took them with him to the country of Yemen. When he passed by Mecca, he wanted to demolish the Kaaba, but they also forbade him from that and told him of the greatness of this house, and that it was built by Abraham, peace be upon him, and that he would have a great affair at the hands of that prophet sent at the end of time. So he glorified it and circumambulated it and covered it with robes, tapestries, and rabbis. Then he returned to Yemen and called its people to Judaism with him. At that time, the religion of Moses, peace be upon him, had those who would… From the guidance before the mission of Jesus, peace be upon him, so the majority of the people of Yemen converted to Judaism with him. The story was mentioned in full by Imam Muhammad bin Ishaq in his book, Al-Seerah, and Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir gave a comprehensive biography of him in his history in which he included many things that we mentioned and what we did not mention. He mentioned that he was the king of Damascus and that whenever he reviewed the horses, they would appear before him from Damascus to Yemen. Then he cited from the path of Abd Al-Razzaq from Muammar from Ibn Abi Dhi’b from Al-Maqburi from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace be upon him, who said: I do not know if the borders are pure for its people or not? I do not know if Tubba was cursed or not? I do not know if Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet or a king? Another said, Was Ezra a prophet or not? Thus, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Dhahrani on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq. Al-Daraqutni said: Abd al-Razzaq was the only one to narrate it. Then Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kurayb on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I do not know whether Ezra was a prophet or not? I do not know whether the accursed one was Tubba’ or not? Then he mentioned what was narrated regarding the prohibition of insulting and cursing him, as will come later, God willing. And it seems that - and God knows best - he was a disbeliever, then he converted to Islam and followed the religion of Moses at the hands of one of the Jewish rabbis of that time, who was on the truth before the mission of Jesus (peace be upon him). He performed Hajj during the time of the Jurhumites, and he was clothed in silk and ink, and six thousand camels were slaughtered near him, and he was honored and respected. Then he returned to Yemen. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated his story in full, through various lengthy and detailed chains of transmission on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abdullah ibn Salam, and Abdullah ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them, and Ka'b al-Ahbar, to whom the reference is made in all of this, and also to Abdullah ibn Salam, who is more established, older, and more knowledgeable. His story was also narrated by Wahb ibn Munabbih and Muhammad ibn Ishaq in the Seerah, as is well-known therein. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mixed up in some contexts the biography of this Tubba’ with the biography of another who came after him by a long time. This Tubba’ referred to in the Qur’an converted his people to Islam at his hands, then when he died, they returned after him to the worship of fire and idols, so God punished them as He mentioned in Surah Saba’. We have already explained their story there, praise and thanks be to God. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Tubba’ covered the Ka’bah, and Sa’id used to forbid cursing him. This Tubba’ is the middle Tubba’, and his name is As’ad Abu Kurayb ibn Malikikarb al-Yamani. They mentioned that he ruled over his people for three hundred and twenty-six years, and there was no one in Himyar who ruled longer than him. He died about seven hundred years before the mission of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). They mentioned that when the two rabbis from the Jews of Medina mentioned to him that this town was the place where a prophet named Ahmad would migrate at the end of time, he composed a poem about that and entrusted it to the people of Medina, who would pass it on and narrate it from generation to generation. Among those who memorized it was Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd, in whose house the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stayed, and it is: I testify that Ahmad is a messenger from God, the Creator of all souls. If my life had been extended to his, I would have been his minister and cousin. I fought his enemies with the sword and relieved his chest of all sorrow Ibn Abi Al-Dunya mentioned that a grave was dug in Sana’a during Islam and two healthy women were found in it, and at their heads was a silver tablet written in gold: This is the grave of Huyayy and Tamis. It was narrated that Huyayy and Tamadur, the daughters of Tubba’, died while bearing witness that there is no god but God and that they do not associate anything with Him. The righteous before them died on that basis. We have also mentioned poetry about this in Surah Saba’. Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that Ka’b used to say about Tubba’ a description of a righteous man: God, the Most High, blamed his people but did not blame him. He said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, used to say: Do not revile Tubba’, for he was a righteous man. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Safwan told us, Al-Walid told us, Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Abu Zur’ah - meaning Amr ibn Jabir Al-Hadrami - who said: I heard Sahl ibn Sa’d Al-Sa’idi, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not revile Tubba’, for he had embraced Islam. It was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad on the authority of Hasan ibn Musa on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah. At-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Abar told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Barzah told us, Mu’ammil ibn Isma’il told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Samak ibn Harb on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: Do not curse Tubba, for he has become Muslim. Abd al-Razzaq also said: Mu’ammar told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b on the authority of al-Maqburi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I do not know whether Tubba was a prophet or not. This chain of transmission was presented earlier on the authority of Ibn Abi Hatim, as Ibn Asakir included it: I do not know whether Tubba was cursed or not. And God knows best. Ibn Asakir narrated it on the authority of Zakariya ibn Yahya al-Badi on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Abdul Razzaq said: Imran Abu Al-Hudhayl told us, Tamim bin Abdul Rahman told me, he said: Ata bin Abi Rabah said: Do not insult Tubba’, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade insulting him, and God Almighty knows best.

This is a false argument and a corrupt semblance, because the afterlife is only on the Day of Resurrection, not in this worldly abode, but after it has passed away and is empty. God will create the worlds anew, and will make the wrongdoers fuel for the fire of Hell, on the day you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. Then God Almighty said, threatening them, warning them, and warning them of His punishment that cannot be repelled, as happened to those like them and their peers among the polytheists who denied the afterlife, such as the people of Tubba’, who are Saba’, when God Almighty destroyed them, ruined their land, scattered them throughout the lands, and dispersed them to scattered fragments, as was mentioned in Surat Saba’, which begins with the denial of the polytheists. 44:38: God Almighty says, informing us of His justice and His transcendence of play, futility, and falsehood, as He, the Most High, says: “And We did not create the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve. So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.” And God Almighty says: Did you then think that We created you in vain and that to Us you would not be returned? So exalted is God, the True King. There is no god but He, Lord of the Noble Throne. Then God Almighty says: Indeed, the Day of Judgment is the appointed time for them all. It is the Day of Resurrection, on which God Almighty will judge between creation, punishing the disbelievers and rewarding the believers. And the saying of God the Almighty: Their appointed time all together means He will gather them all, the first of them and the last of them. On a Day when no protector will avail another protector at all meaning no relative will benefit a relative, as in His saying the Almighty: Then when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask about one another and His saying, may He be glorified and exalted: And no friend will ask a friend * They will see them meaning no brother will ask about his condition while he sees them with his own eyes. And the saying of God the Almighty: Nor will they be aided meaning no relative will aid his relative, nor will His aid come to him from outside. Then He said: Except him upon whom God has mercy meaning nothing will benefit on that Day except the mercy of God the Almighty to His creation. Indeed, it is He who is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful meaning He is the Exalted in Might, the Possessor of vast mercy.

44:43: God Almighty says, informing us of the punishment with which He will punish the unbelievers who deny meeting Him: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinner. The sinner means in his words and actions, and he is the unbeliever. More than one person has mentioned that it is Abu Jahl, and there is no doubt that he is included in this verse, but it is not specific to him. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam ibn al-Harith, that Abu al-Darda’ was teaching a man, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * Is the food of the sinner, and he said, The food of the orphan, so Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, said, Say, ‘Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is the food of the wicked,’ meaning he has no food other than it. Mujahid said, If a drop of it fell to the ground, it would ruin the livelihood of the people of the earth. A similar hadith was previously transmitted with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. His statement, Like molten metal, they said, Like cloudy oil, “Boils in the bellies * Like the boiling of scalding water,” meaning from its heat and badness. His statement, Seize him, meaning the disbeliever. It has been reported that when God Almighty says to the guards, Seize him, seventy thousand of them rush to him. His statement, So ride him, means drive him by pulling and pushing him on his back. Mujahid said, So ride him, meaning, take him and push him. Al-Farazdaq said: The generous are not like your father until you return to Atiya To the middle of Hellfire meaning its middle Then they will pour over his head the torment of scalding water as God Almighty says: Boiling water will be poured over their heads, melting thereby that which is in their bellies and also their skins and it was mentioned earlier that the angel will hit him with an iron whip, splitting his brains, then the scalding water will be poured over his head and will descend into his body, and what is in his stomach of his intestines will flow out until it comes out from his ankles. May God Almighty protect us from that. And God Almighty says: "Taste. Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble" meaning say that to him in a mocking and rebuking way. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: meaning you are neither mighty nor noble. Al-Amawi said in his book, Al-Maghazi: Asbat bin Muhammad told us, Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met Abu Jahl, may God curse him, and said: God the Most High has commanded me to say to you, ‘It is better for you, then better, then better for you, then better.’ So he took his garment from his hand and said: “Neither you nor your companion can do anything to me. You know that I can protect the people of Al-Batha’, and I am the Almighty, the Generous.” So God killed him on the Day of Badr, humiliated him, and taunted him with his word, and revealed: Taste, for indeed, you are the Almighty, the Generous. And the words of God the Almighty: This is what you were in doubt about are like His words: The Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, He will summon * This is the Fire which you used to deny * Is this magic, or do you not see? That is why God the Most High said here: This is what you were in doubt about.

44:51: When the Almighty mentioned the state of the wretched, He followed it with mentioning the happy ones, and for this reason the Qur’an is called Mathani repeated. He said: Indeed, the righteous meaning of God in this world will be in a secure position meaning in the Hereafter, which is Paradise. They will be safe therein from death and expulsion, and from all worry, sadness, anxiety, fatigue and exhaustion, and from Satan and his plots and all other afflictions and calamities in gardens and springs This is in contrast to what those people will be in of the tree of Zaqqum and drinking scalding water. And the Almighty said: They will wear fine silk which is fine silk like shirts and the like and heavy brocade which is what has shine and luster, such as feathers and what is worn over the tops of cloth facing each other meaning on couches, no one of them will sit with his back to another. And the Almighty’s saying: Likewise, and We have married them to fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes. That is, this gift is in addition to what We have given them of beautiful wives, the fair maidens whom no man or jinn has touched before them. “As if they were rubies and coral.” Is the reward for good [anything] but good? Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Nuh ibn Habib told us, Nasr ibn Muzahim al-Attar told us, Umar ibn Saad told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Nuh, who said: If a fair maiden spat into a deep sea, the water would be sweet because of the sweetness of her saliva. God the Almighty says: {Therein they will call for every kind of fruit, secure} meaning, whatever type of fruit they request, it will be brought to them and they will be secure from its interruption or withholding. Rather, it will be brought to them whenever they desire. And His statement: {They will not taste death therein except the first death} This is an exception that confirms the negation, for it is an interrupted exception. Its meaning is that they will never taste death therein, as it is proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Death will be brought in the form of a white ram and will be stopped between Paradise and Hellfire, then it will be slaughtered, then it will be said: O people of Paradise, eternity and no death. O people of Hellfire, eternity and no death.” The hadith was previously mentioned in Surah Maryam (blessings and peace of God be upon her). Abdul Razzaq said: Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Muslim al-Aghar, on the authority of Abu Sa’id and Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “It will be said to the people of Paradise: ‘You will have health and never fall ill, you will live and never die, you will enjoy comfort and never feel miserable, and you will be young and never grow old.’” Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and Abd ibn Humayd, both on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq. This is how Abu Ishaq says it. The people of Iraq say Abu Muslim al-Aghar, and the people of Medina say Abu Abdullah al-Aghar. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud al-Sijistani said: Ahmad ibn Hafs told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, on the authority of al-Hajjaj (i.e. Ibn Hajjaj), on the authority of Ubadah, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever fears God will enter Paradise, enjoy comfort therein and never feel miserable, live therein and never die, his clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Yahya told us, Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid told us, Salim ibn Abdullah al-Raqqi told us, Mus`ab ibn Ibrahim told us, Imran ibn al-Rabi` al-Kufi told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Ansari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Do the people of Paradise sleep? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Sleep is the brother of death, and the people of Paradise do not sleep. This is how Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir. Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Sadaqa al-Misri narrated to us, al-Miqdam ibn Dawud narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Sleep is the brother of death, and the people of Paradise do not sleep. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Al-Fadl ibn Ya’qub narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Faryabi narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him, who said: It was said, O Messenger of God, do the people of Paradise sleep? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: No, sleep is the brother of death. Then he said: We do not know of anyone who narrated it on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadir on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him except al-Thawri, nor on the authority of al-Thawri except al-Faryabi. This is what he said, and something different has been mentioned before, and God knows best. And the Almighty said: {And saved them from the punishment of Hellfire} meaning, along with this great and lasting bliss, He saved them, delivered them, and removed them from the painful punishment in the depths of Hellfire, so they obtained what they wanted and saved them from what they feared. For this reason, the Almighty said: {Blessing from your Lord. That is what is feared} meaning, this was only due to His favor and kindness to them, as is proven in the Sahih on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Work, strive hard, and strive for the path of righteousness, and know that no one’s deeds will admit him into Paradise. They said: Not even you, O Messenger of God? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Not even I, unless God covers me with His mercy and favor. And the Almighty said: {So We have only made it easy in your language that they might be reminded} meaning, We have only made this Qur’an that We have revealed easy, clear, and distinct in your language, which is the most eloquent, most distinguished, and most exalted of languages, that they might remember meaning that they might understand and know. Then, when despite this clarity and explanation, there were still people who disbelieved, opposed, and were obstinate, God the Almighty said to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, comforting him and promising him victory, and threatening those who denied him with destruction and ruin: Then wait, that is, wait, for they are waiting, that is, they will work for whoever will have victory, triumph, and supremacy in this world and the hereafter. For it will be for you, O Muhammad, and for your brothers among the prophets and messengers and those who follow you among the believers, as God the Almighty said: God has decreed, ‘I will surely prevail, I and My messengers,’ (al-An’am 2:17). And God the Almighty said: “Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand * The Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the worst home.”

And the Almighty said: They will wear fine silk which is fine silk like shirts and the like and heavy brocade which is what has shine and luster, such as feathers and what is worn over the tops of cloth facing each other meaning on couches, no one of them will sit with his back to another. And the Almighty’s saying: Likewise, and We have married them to fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes. That is, this gift is in addition to what We have given them of beautiful wives, the fair maidens whom no man or jinn has touched before them. “As if they were rubies and coral.” Is the reward for good [anything] but good? God the Almighty says: {Therein they will call for every kind of fruit, secure} meaning, whatever type of fruit they request, it will be brought to them and they will be secure from its interruption or withholding. Rather, it will be brought to them whenever they desire. And His statement: {They will not taste death therein except the first death} This is an exception that confirms the negation, for it is an interrupted exception. Its meaning is that they will never taste death therein, as it is proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Death will be brought in the form of a white ram and will be stopped between Paradise and Hellfire, then it will be slaughtered, then it will be said: O people of Paradise, eternity and no death. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: No, sleep is the brother of death. This is what he said, and something different has been mentioned before, and God knows best.
